summary:
Held 0 of today's 10 biggest US movers.

• 6 upside misses — SMCI +10%, CRL +9%, BE +7%, DDOG +6%, CIEN +6%. These cleared the universe screen but no strategy picked them up; the morning brief either filtered them on a catalyst/RSI/earnings rule or had nothing positive to trigger an entry.

• 4 downside moves (T -6%, DXCM -6%, NFLX -5%, CMG -5%) are unreachable on a long-only basket — no mechanism to express a short or pair-trade.

• Most instructive miss: SMCI (+9.55%) — Super Micro pre-announced fiscal Q1'27 results: revenue $18.5-19.5B (above prior guidance) and gross margin 12.0-12.5% (was 10.4-10.8%), on strong AI server demand. The 35.57 close matches Oct 21's close, so the move likely dates from that session. Why we passed: Outside any active strategy's universe: SMCI is a volatile mid/large-cap AI-hardware name that no strategy lists. It was also a pre-market guidance-driven gap, so any post-open momentum or news-reactive signal would have fired after the move was largely priced in.

top_movers.catalyst: Super Micro pre-announced fiscal Q1'27 results: revenue $18.5-19.5B (above prior guidance) and gross margin 12.0-12.5% (was 10.4-10.8%), on strong AI server demand. The 35.57 close matches Oct 21's close, so the move likely dates from that session.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: SMCI is a volatile mid/large-cap AI-hardware name that no strategy lists. It was also a pre-market guidance-driven gap, so any post-open momentum or news-reactive signal would have fired after the move was largely priced in.
top_movers.suggestion: Add SMCI and similar high-beta AI-server names (DELL, VRT, CLS) to the momentum-trader universe. Also let the news-reactive gate admit pre-announcements that raise guidance, with a gap of +5% or more and volume at least 1.5x average.

top_movers.catalyst: No company-specific news found for Oct 22; Q3 earnings aren't due until Nov 4. The +9.3% move is likely a sector rally (CRO/biotech tools, possibly peer earnings) or an analyst action.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: CRL is a ~$17B mid-cap life-science tools/CRO name that no strategy lists. With no pre-market catalyst, a news-reactive filter had nothing to trigger on, and a momentum screen wouldn't have flagged it before the intraday move.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily 'dynamic mid-cap' universe slice (S&P 400/500 names with price ≥ $20 and 20-day avg volume ≥ 500k) to the momentum strategy, so a ≥ +5% day on volume ≥ 2× average is evaluated rather than skipped for lack of membership.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed catalyst for 2026-10-22. BE (Bloom Energy, fuel cells for AI data-centre power) is a high-beta name that fell ~9% on Oct 14 and probably rebounded with the AI-power theme.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. BE is a volatile mid/large-cap clean-energy/AI-power name that no strategy lists. A +7% rebound without a clear news hook also wouldn't trigger a news-reactive entry.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta AI-power/energy names such as BE to the momentum universe, with a dynamic add rule: ADV above $200M and 20-day ATR above 5%. Cap position size to limit volatility risk.

top_movers.catalyst: Continued rebound on AI-demand analyst upgrades (Bernstein to Outperform, PT $350; Mizuho/Barclays/Morgan Stanley PT raises). Exact date of each note unclear. No earnings; next report is Nov 4.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DDOG is a mid/large-cap software name that no strategy lists. It also had a multi-day run (+7.8% on Oct 21), so an RSI or extension filter would likely have excluded it.
top_movers.suggestion: Add high-beta software/AI-infrastructure names such as DDOG, SNOW and NET to the momentum universe. Also add an analyst-upgrade news trigger that allows entry on a ≥+5% day with volume ≥1.5× the 20-day average.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed Oct 22 news found. Likely a sector move in optical/AI-networking names. Ciena is a high-beta AI-datacenter optical play and has been volatile since its Q3 FY26 earnings.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CIEN is a roughly $50B mid/large-cap networking name, and no strategy's universe includes it. A +5.7% move with no company-specific catalyst also gives news-reactive logic nothing to trigger on.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a dynamic universe slot to momentum-trader. It would admit US tech/networking names above $10B market cap with a 20-day average dollar volume above $200M, and it could be seeded from the prior day's top sector-ETF constituents.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed same-day catalyst. Likely a continued diagnostics/life-science tools sector rally and BioInsight software launch sentiment, with Q3 earnings due Oct 29.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: ILMN is a ~$40B mid/large-cap life-science tools name that no strategy's universe lists. The move was also sector and sentiment driven with no discrete news event for a news-reactive filter to catch.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a daily scan that lets any US name with ≥5% close-to-close gain on ≥1.5× average volume into the momentum-trader universe for the next session, which would catch ILMN-style sector-rally leaders outside the static list.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely AT&T Q3 earnings reaction (it usually reports around Oct 22). I couldn't find coverage confirming the date or the cause of the -6.45% drop, so this is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: T is a mega-cap, low-beta telecom, probably excluded as a defensive, low-volatility name. An earnings gap-down at the open also leaves no entry, and the bot has no short capability.
top_movers.suggestion: No actionable change for the long-only book. Optionally, add large-cap defensive names to the news-reactive universe so post-earnings gap-downs can trigger an exit or avoid-list flag.

top_movers.catalyst: Abbott cut its diabetes-care growth outlook to low-to-mid single digits, raising CGM demand and competition worries, plus pre-earnings positioning ahead of DexCom's Q3 report on Oct 29. Search results dated the ~6% drop Oct 21, so the date is unconfirmed.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: DXCM is a mid-cap medtech name that no strategy lists. The drop was also a read-through from a peer's guidance, not a DXCM-specific news or gap signal, so a news-reactive filter would not have fired.
top_movers.suggestion: Add a healthcare/medtech sleeve to the news-reactive universe, e.g. DXCM, PODD and ABT, and trigger it on a peer-guidance read-through with a ≥5% close-to-close drop on ≥1.5× average volume; otherwise no change, since the bot can't short.

top_movers.catalyst: Likely continued post-earnings selling after Netflix's Oct 20 Q3 report (the stock has fallen after each of its last four reports). I couldn't confirm a fresh Oct 22 headline, so this is partly inferred.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe: NFLX is a large-cap, but no strategy lists it. The drop also came two sessions after the earnings gap, so a gap-up/news-reactive filter would have seen no fresh trigger, and a long-only bot can't short the weakness.
top_movers.suggestion: Add NFLX and similar large-cap streamers to the mean-reversion universe, gated by a post-earnings rule: after a gap-down of 7% or more, wait 2 sessions and enter only if the close is above the prior low and RSI(14) is below 30.

top_movers.catalyst: No confirmed driver found. Q3 earnings aren't due until Oct 28, so this looks like a pre-earnings selloff tied to food-safety (Cyclospora) and weak-traffic worries, not a company announcement.
top_movers.miss_reason: Outside any active strategy's universe. CMG is a large-cap restaurant name that no strategy lists. With no earnings or news gap, a -5% drift would also not trip a gap or news-reactive trigger.
top_movers.suggestion: Add large-cap consumer-discretionary names like CMG to the mean-reversion universe, with a pre-earnings blackout filter that skips entries within 5 trading days of the report date.
